evidence: The ask is a full multi-user product, not a tweak. instruction.md:1 asks to build HireOps from nothing with a per-job pipeline board, recruiter-candidate conversations and several concurrent users. instruction.md:3 requires one-stage moves, a shared within-stage order, Interview capacity, refusals that name the colleague who made the conflicting change, all-or-nothing multi-card moves and undo. Further paragraphs require live updates within 15 s that leave focus and drafts alone, paged history, per-person unread and seen state, drafts that survive sign-out, and a candidate view that withholds staff data. instruction.md:15 requires a Node/Express/SQLite server with durable /app/app.db and DB_PATH, plus restart persistence. hireops_rules.md sections 1-9 add roles (401/403/404), versioned 409 conflicts, an Activity log and seed loading. The template instruction.md is only 'CHANGE_ME', so all of this is task-authored. task.toml calls the task difficulty 'hard', and its difficulty_explanation matches the brief. The smallest submission that satisfies the brief is therefore a real server-backed, multi-role, concurrent app; a static page, a single CRUD screen or a mock cannot satisfy it. The grading also enforces this. Gate hro_gate_render (gates/render/judge.toml) requires a wrong-password refusal and a real sign-in to a usable workspace, and says 'A static picture or only a health response is insufficient'. Gate hro_gate_shared (gates/constraints/judge.toml:20-27) requires a UI add-candidate that survives a reload and that the Observer reads back in an independent browser context; 'A static seed response, a no-op success message or a browser-only save does not satisfy the gate.' Both gates have weight 0.0 in scoring.toml, so failing either makes the reward 0 (score.py:41,48). functional/prompt.md:11-13 and visual/prompt.md:11-12 repeat that backend check: a static shell gives every functional criterion 0 and every visual Likert score its minimum. functional/prompt.md:13 says 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control', so a dead feature cannot earn credit for refusing. There are 44 functional criteria worth 61.0 in total weight, and scoring.toml:11 sets a functional floor of 0.05. The scoring policy is byte-identical to the template and was not altered. Golden: solution/app is about 1,400 lines across server and client (index.js 450, board.js 373, threads.js 224, app.js 221), and its hashes match the raw-evidence-index scripted golden run. Colderwater lessons that bear on this row were checked: lesson 4 (gates stay simple: sign in, a server-backed write and an independent readback, with the strictness kept in scored rows) holds, and the policy's 'gates must exclude convincing dead apps' holds through the independent-context Observer readback. Lesson 1 (no hidden requirements) has no instance here, because every scored behaviour cited above appears in the brief or the rules notes.
counterexample: Weak-app probe, reasoned from source and not run. Consider a login plus a single add-candidate/open-job CRUD screen backed by SQLite, with correct 403s for the Observer and no moves, conversations or live updates. It passes both gates. It can plausibly earn hro_job_open (1), hro_add_candidate (1) and hro_add_email_rules (1). It can also earn hro_refusal_status (1), because that row counts only replays that were refused, and an Observer add-candidate or open-job replay refused with 403 satisfies it. That is about 4/61 = 0.066 functional, above the 0.05 floor. Rows that need a move, multi-card move or undo control (hro_observer_readonly, hro_anonymous, hro_candidate_no_staff) and hro_restart (which needs seeded notes, messages, unread counts and activity) should fail. With visual Likert scores of about 2-3 on a board-only UI and polish at 0, the reward is roughly 0.6*0.066 + 0.2*(0.25 to 0.5) = 0.09 to 0.14. Without the refusal_status point the stub falls to 3/61 = 0.049, below the floor, and earns 0. This is partial credit for real partial work against a golden near 1.0, so the task still clearly separates a real build from a stub, and it is not a row-7 defect. It is noted because the stub could land at the bottom of the 0.1-0.7 target band. Conforming-alternative probe: no conforming app fails because of what the brief asks. Routes, labels and layout are explicitly left to the builder (hireops_rules.md preamble; instruction.md: 'layout and names are yours'), so this row does not penalize any valid design.
suggested_fix: No change to the task is required for row 7. To close the risk, include a CRUD-only stub (login + add-candidate/open-job + role 403s, no board moves or conversations) in the planned reward-discrimination runtime record, and confirm its measured reward is about 0.1 or less, well below the golden. If it measures higher, tighten the scored criteria, never the weights or floor (lesson 2).
